taxonomic_note: Accepted by Kew/POWO; Old World native and introduced in Texas.
look_here_first: First check the stout, relatively dense, many-flowered spikelets and ANNUAL habit. Under 10–20× look for distinctive craterlike/wartlike GLANDS on inflorescence branches, pedicels, glume or lemma keels (variable; not all photos show them). Fresh plants may smell strong when crushed, but odor is a secondary clue.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Kew/POWO treats Texas as introduced. ITIS/USDA-derived status treats continental U.S. populations as introduced.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Wild occurrence does not equal native status.

morphology_keys.comparison_training: Eragrostis intermedia: Perennial with a finer transparent panicle and no conspicuous gland-dotted coarse spikelets. Eragrostis trichodes: Tall perennial with huge effuse panicle and long sheath-throat hairs.
morphology_keys.field_teaching_note: Kew/GrassBase and FNA describe annual culms, many-flowered flattened spikelets and variable crateriform glands on branches/pedicels or lemmas. A lack of visible glands in a photo is not strong evidence of their absence.
morphology_keys.crew_recognition_summary: STINKGRASS = annual with comparatively large dense multi-flowered spikelets, often with glandular pits. Smell alone isn't ID.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Whole annual clump including base and attached inflorescence.
Close mature spikelet face showing many stacked florets with a mm ruler.
True macro of crateriform gland pits on branchlet, lemma keel or pedicel.
Collar/ligule closeup plus an adjacent red lovegrass comparison if found.

comparisons.key_distinctions: E. secundiflora can also have large dense spikelets but is a perennial and has different panicle architecture; glands on branchlets/lemma keel are especially worth checking in cilianensis. E. intermedia / E. spectabilis usually look more open with scattered smaller spikelets. Other introduced annual lovegrasses may require dissection; distinguish E. pectinacea using mature spikelet structure and glands, not odor only.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Eragrostis cilianensis — follow the real-photo field cues
steps: START with the source-verified 10-mm montage of actual leaf sheaths and blades: identify the OUTSIDE blade–sheath junction in multiple angles.

OPEN the blade away from its sheathing base: the new source-verified 3-mm macro shows a short whitish fringe of the TRUE LIGULE on its inner side. Do not confuse it with long hairs at the outside sheath mouth or collar.
Find a low to medium annual grass clump with relatively coarse seedhead compared with the fine airy natives.
Look at the chunky flat spikelets along a branch; identify one entire spikelet before counting florets.
Use 10–20× and a side-lit macro to find wartlike gland pits on branches, pedicels or individual florets. Missing tiny visible glands is NOT negative proof.

NODE GLAND PHOTO LEAD: Harry Rose's separately source-identified E. cilianensis node1 NWS photo shows a broad brownish ring immediately below the culm node (Commons CC BY 2.0; Flickr photo 27519504922). The individual crateriform glands are NOT resolved; original image has GPS EXIF and must be locally archived/scrubbed before learner installation. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Eragrostis_cilianensis_node1_NWS_-_Flickr_-_Macleay_Grass_Man.jpg . NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO, annotation_pending.

field_id_short_tiles.short: Annual tuft with chunky, many-flowered spikelets; smell is only supporting.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Trace an attached flowering culm to a fibrous annual base (FNA commonly 15–45(–65) cm). Panicle may be condensed OR open, so neither density nor odor alone establishes stinkgrass. Check mature spikelets and glands. Existing overview photographs do not prove roots or microscopic glands.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · OPEN THE TRUE LIGULE
field_id_short_tiles.short: True ligule is a ~0.4–0.8 mm FRINGE OF HAIRS.
field_id_short_tiles.details: At the inner blade–sheath junction, distinguish the short true ciliate ligule from the much longer hairs at the outer sheath mouth (to ~5 mm in FNA). Gallery index 3 is an OUTER collar context photograph, index 4 is the blade–sheath junction montage, and index 5 is Stefan.lefnaer's source-identified TRUE inner ligule hair-fringe macro with a printed 3-mm scale. Index 6 is a DIFFERENT species (red lovegrass) and must never illustrate this ligule. The image does not independently validate a 0.4–0.8-mm measurement or a Texas locality.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL SOURCE-LABELLED LIGULE PHOTO — PRECISE LENGTH NOT PIXEL-VERIFIED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · PANICLE BRANCHES AND GLAND PITS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Stout branches ~0.4–5 cm; craterlike glands often on nodes, pedicels or lemma keels.
field_id_short_tiles.details: FNA describes panicles mostly 5–16(–20) cm long, with stiff primary branches and short pedicels ~0.2–3 mm. Inspect several nodes, pedicels and lemma keels at 10–20× for small crateriform gland pits. Glands vary and may be invisible on a normal field photo; do not draw a gland arrow until actual pits are resolved.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · MEASURE ONE MATURE SPIKELET
field_id_short_tiles.short: Flattened spikelets mostly 6–20 × 2–4 mm, commonly 10–40 florets.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Isolate one mature spikelet and count overlapping florets in TWO ranks, rather than mistaking an entire flowering branch for one spikelet. FNA's 6–20 mm range is narrower than some global treatments; use the cited treatment and a real millimeter ruler. Existing Harry Rose spikelet photo teaches gross structure, not independently calibrated floret count.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · SEPARATE GLUMES, LEMMA AND PALEA
field_id_short_tiles.short: Lower glume ~1.2–2 mm (usually 1 vein); upper ~1.2–2.6 mm (often 3); lemma ~2–2.8 mm, 3-veined, AWNLESS.
field_id_short_tiles.details: At 20–40× remove the two short basal glumes and expose a mature fertile floret. FNA describes three-veined lemmas with often 1–3 crateriform glands on the keel; palea ~1.2–2.1 mm, its two keels rough and sometimes ciliate. No long lemma awn. Published anatomical ranges are NOT measurements of gallery pixels. No current panel shows separated, calibrated glumes, lemma and palea: this teaching tile intentionally has NO image reference until a real dissection is added.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · CENTRAL TEXAS LOOK-ALIKES + RELEASE GATE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Separate native perennial red lovegrass from introduced annual stinkgrass using base + glandular spikelet.
field_id_short_tiles.details: E. secundiflora is perennial, often with clustered reddish spikelets but red color overlaps; E. spectabilis has a loose spreading cloud; E. intermedia has a finer open panicle; other introduced annual Eragrostis require ripe floret examination.
